title: C1613 — Camshaft Position Bank 2 Sensor 1 (CMP21)
introduction:
I read this connector reference like a seating chart: the drawing shows the cavity labels, and the matching table rows identify the circuits assigned to them. Start with the connector identity and housing information, then use the face drawing, pin assignments and pigtail catalog together. The circuit functions distinguish the sensor connection, signal return and buffered sensor-power supply—different jobs sharing the same small housing.

This is a reference for reading the connections. It does not teach physical access, probing, electrical diagnosis or replacement. Viewing direction, gauge convention and the meanings of Size and Used are not defined here; keep those fields literal rather than turning them into test or repair instructions.

edits.why: I use the tall rounded outline, broad rectangular projection on the left and smaller projection on the right to recognize the drawing as displayed. Match its cavity labels to the Cavity column below. These are housing features; their release or locking functions are not identified. The displayed arrangement alone does not establish which side of a physical connector to view.

Read across each cavity row to connect its circuit identity with the color, gauge, function and terminal entry. The Function column explains the electrical role; a circuit identifier is an address, not a verdict that the circuit works. Use the map when reading the matching wiring information, and use a separate diagnostic procedure before drawing conclusions from measurements.

A pigtail is a connector with attached wire leads. Each catalog row ties its kit entry to a service part, engineering shell and listed construction details. The matching shell entries do not establish that the kits are interchangeable or explain which to choose. This table provides a parts cross-reference, not a replacement or splicing procedure.
